issues: Only a flat loading screen is visible; the Apollo spacecraft, launch pad, service tower, and environment are not rendered.
The visible loading message does not establish the requested cinematic composition or any scene detail.
Lighting, materials, shadows, floodlights, steam, and dawn atmosphere cannot be evaluated because the scene is absent.
fixes: Hide the loading overlay and display the WebGL canvas after the scene, camera, and renderer finish initializing.

issues: The service tower is clipped by the top edge of the frame.
The camera is close to eye level rather than a cinematic low-angle wide shot.
No distinct rising sun or direct dawn light source is visible.
The floodlights are small and their illumination is not clearly readable.
The vented steam is heavily overexposed and lacks visible directional shape.
The simplified background buildings and ground do little to reinforce the wide launch-pad setting.
fixes: Lower the camera to roughly 0.6 units above the pad and tilt upward slightly.
Reduce the camera FOV or dolly backward so the entire tower remains inside the viewport.
Add a visible warm sun sprite just above the horizon and align a directional light with it.
Increase the floodlight spot intensities and add small cool-white emissive lamp meshes at their fixtures.
Reduce the steam material opacity and emissive intensity so its plume structure remains visible.
Subtly increase directional and ambient light contrast while keeping the rocket’s white surfaces below clipping.

issues: The foreground launch pad is heavily underexposed and loses most surface detail.

The scene dressing is sparse, with little recognizable launch-pad infrastructure beyond the tower and lights.
fixes: Increase the pad and foreground lighting so the platform, flame trench, and nearby ground remain visible.
Add a visible sun disc just above the horizon and align its glow with the warm directional light.
Reduce the steam material opacity and emissive brightness, and vary the particle scale for softer vapor.
Add subtle roughness, metalness, and normal-map variation to the tower, rocket, and concrete pad materials.
Add low-profile launch-pad details such as service conduits, platforms, railings, and cable runs.
